transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21 15:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Elena Fischer (Helioinformatics Head of ML), Sofia Moreno (NLP Lead), Raj Patel (SRE), Tom Barnes (Product), Ibrahim Kaur (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
Helioinformatics wants to run a 4-week POC to validate open-model options for domain-specific, multilingual clinical summarization and entity extraction. Primary success criteria: latency < 400ms p95 for 512-token context in Dedicated mode or < 700ms hosted with caching; extraction F1 >= 0.88 on in-house test set; cost target <$0.35 per 1k tokens. Discussed model shortlist (Llama variants, Mistral-ish open models, Mosaic/Redwood-verified builds), quantization tradeoffs, multilingual coverage (EN/DE/ES/PT), and timeline for bench runs. Security and VPC peering required; SOC2 docs requested. Next steps and action items enumerated.

Topics:
- Success criteria and KPIs
- Workload sizing (qps, token lengths, concurrency)
- Bench plan and metrics
- Open-model shortlist and tradeoffs (quality vs latency vs cost)
- Multilingual/domain adaptions and evaluation sets
- Deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)
- Security/compliance asks

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): all right, hello everyone, thanks for joining. uh this is Maya from Redwood, with Diego our solutions engineer. today's goal is to scope the POC: success criteria, workloads, and pick a model shortlist to benchmark.
[00:12] Elena (Helioinformatics): thanks Maya. We have a fairly tight timeline; product wants a recommendation in four weeks. main use case is clinical note summarization and structured entity extraction from multi-lingual intake forms. we care a lot about precision on medications and dosages.
[00:25] Diego (Redwood SE): got it. can you give us the traffic profile? i.e., qps, average and p95 token lengths, and peak concurrency?
[00:35] Sofia (NLP Lead): sure. average request is 350 tokens in, 120 tokens out. p95 input size is ~900 tokens for long notes. baseline qps is 4, peaks up to 18 for batch jobs. concu... concurrency target we'd like to support is 12 concurrent streams with p95 latency targets.
[00:55] Raj (SRE): from infra perspective we can provision a VPC peering window next week; we do have strict egress rules and require KMS-backed encryption for any private deployment.
[01:05] Maya: perfect. so initial success criteria proposal: quality: extraction F1 >= 0.88 for entities, summary ROUGE-L or human score within X% of our internal baseline. latency: p95 <= 400ms for 512 token context in Dedicated, or <= 700ms for hosted with caching. cost: target <$0.35 per 1k tokens. are those realistic?
[01:20] Elena: the quality thresholds are non-negotiable; cost is a soft target. timeline for quality check is 3 weeks, we want to start bench runs within 4 business days.
[01:30] Diego: ok noted. for model shortlist we typically recommend a spectrum: a high-quality large model, a mid-size efficient model, and a small low-cost variant. given domain and multilingual requirements, our proposed shortlist is: 1) Llama-3-70B-open (finetune variant), 2) Mistral-inp-style-34B-open (or equivalent), 3) Llama-3-13B-quantized, 4) bloomz-like multilingual baseline. each has tradeoffs on latency and multilingual out-of-the-box capability.
[01:55] Tom (Product): can you unpack the multilingual picks? we need solid DE and PT support, not just EN/ES.
[02:03] Diego: bloomz-like is naturally multilingual but lower on hallucination resistance; the 70B Llama variant with light domain fine-tuning gave the best English clinical extract results in our internal tests, and we saw decent DE performance after a small multilingual adaptor step. the 13B quantized gives big cost wins but you'll likely lose 3-6% absolute F1 in extraction.
[02:28] Sofia: what about instruction-tuning quality? we rely on structured output and tool-style calls; some models struggle with consistent JSON outputs.
[02:36] Maya: that's an important point. we'll include structured-output evals in the bench suite and a function-calling consistency metric. Diego, can we add a test that measures JSON validity and field-level precision?
[02:46] Diego: yes, we'll add schema conformance checks and per-field precision/recall.
[02:50] Ibrahim (Security): SOC2 and encryption are mandatory. also we want audit logs for token-level tracing off by default. can Redwood support customer-side KMS in the private deployment?
[03:00] Maya: yes, Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit log export. Hosted can offer encrypted-at-rest and in-transit but not customer KM S in the same way. we'll send the SOC2 pack.
[03:12] Raj: for hosted tests we'll need egress accounting and we prefer to run heavy perf runs in Dedicated to avoid noisy neighbors.
[03:20] Diego: makes sense — dedicated pools give predictable p95 latency and throughput. For bench plan: propose 3 phases: 1) smoke and correctness (small sample, structural tests), 2) throughput/latency with synthetic traffic matching your token distribution and concurrency, 3) quality sweep on 5k held-out samples across 4 languages. total bench compute estimate: ~72 GPU-hours per large model variant to get reliable p95 and cost numbers.
[03:48] Elena: that compute estimate, is that for 70B only?
[03:52] Diego: yes, 70B needs the most. 34B about 28 GPU-hours, 13B about 8-12 GPU-hours. We'll provide cost estimate and exact instance types — note quantized runs are cheaper but may need additional validation.
[04:05] Tom: can you explain caching impacts — our summaries often reuse the same patient prompt prefix.
[04:10] Diego: sure, prefix/KV cache can reduce token compute for repeated system prompts by 20-40% depending on prompt reuse pattern. We'll run bench variants with and without prefix cache in Dedicated to show realistic cost delta. note that cache effects are less pronounced for long, unique notes.
[04:27] Sofia: on quality metrics: besides F1, we'd like strict dosage detection — a custom metric that tracks unit normalization (mg, mcg) and out-of-range flags.
[04:36] Maya: add that as a custom eval in the bench template. we'll include a small normalization scorer.
[04:41] Elena: timeline check: start bench in 4 days, initial results within one week, final report and recommendation in 3 weeks. are there blockers?
[04:51] Diego: blockers: we need your 5k eval set (labeled), and a stable test subnet for Dedicated peering; also confirm whether you want to run any finetune/LoRA steps vs pure zero-shot/adapter evals. finetuning will add time.
[05:05] Elena: we can do light LoRA on the 70B if it helps reach F1 target, but only if it fits the timeline. can you give an estimate for LoRA cycle?
[05:12] Diego: a quick LoRA cycle (adapter training) on 70B for this domain typically takes 10-18 hours of GPU time plus validation, so add ~2-3 days to the timeline. we'll scope it as an optional phase; primary POC will be eval-only.
[05:25] Ibrahim: legal: we need a data handling addendum before we share PHI-like samples. can you route that to legal?
[05:31] Maya: yes — i'll loop in our legal and send the DPA + security questionnaire after this call.
[05:36] Raj: small note: network egress to hosted endpoints may be limited by our cloud provider; we'll likely prefer Dedicated in their region.
[05:43] Diego: ok. for deployment recommendation at end of POC we'll map cost/latency curves: hosted (fast to start, higher variability), Dedicated (predictable SLA), Private (maximum control + CMK).
[05:57] Sofia: question — what about model variants you mentioned like mosaic or mismatched names; are these fully supported?
[06:02] Maya: some open models have build quirks we call out in our catalog — e.g., tokenizer edge cases, broken eos tokens, or kv cache behaviour. we'll share a short compatibility matrix in the bench template that flags things like tokenizer segmentation for DE/PT.
[06:18] Tom: interop with our downstream pipeline — can Redwood stream tokens as they're generated so our frontend can begin rendering partial summaries?
[06:25] Diego: yes, streaming is supported for hosted and dedicated. for very low-latency streaming you may prefer dedicated in-region.
[06:33] Elena: ok final recap then.
[06:36] Maya: recap: Redwood to send bench template + top-10 prompt list and compatibility matrix by 2026-05-24; Diego to stand up perf scripts and estimates by 2026-05-26; Helio to share labeled 5k eval set (redacted if needed) by 2026-05-25; schedule 2-hr bench run 2026-05-28 with SE. Security/legal: DPA and SOC2 to be shared; Helio to confirm VPC peering window. action items in notes.
[06:58] Elena: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:01] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up via email and put the bench plan into the shared drive.

--- End ---
